name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
principle: External input is used to construct a file or directory path without neutralizing special path elements. Attackers can make the path resolve outside the intended directory and read, write, delete, or execute unexpected files.
detection_signals: request.getParameter(...) or argv[...] concatenated into new File(...), FileInputStream(...), FileOutputStream(...), Files.readAllBytes(...), Files.delete(...)
user-controlled string passed to fopen(...), open(...), std::ifstream(...), std::ofstream(...), remove(...), unlink(...)
Paths.get(base, input) or base.resolve(input) used without normalize()/toRealPath()/getCanonicalPath() and a base-directory check
realpath(...), File.getCanonicalPath(), or Path.toRealPath() called but result is not checked against canonical base directory
path.startsWith(base) or string prefix check performed before canonicalization
replace("../", ""), replace("..\\", ""), regex stripping of separators, or blacklist-only path filtering
URLDecoder.decode(...), servlet decoding, or custom percent-decoding occurs after path validation
negative_signals: Path baseReal = base.toRealPath(); Path target = baseReal.resolve(input).toRealPath(...); target.startsWith(baseReal) is checked before file use
File.getCanonicalPath() applied to both base and target, then targetCanonical is verified under baseCanonical plus separator
input is an ID used in a fixed ID-to-filename map; raw path strings are not accepted
allowlist regex permits only simple filenames and rejects '/', '\\', ':', '..', and unexpected extensions
Java NIO uses LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS where symlink traversal is not allowed, plus a post-resolution base check
false_defense_traps: Removing '../' or '..\\' without canonicalizing the final path
Blocking '/' but allowing '\\' or platform-specific separators
Using normalize() only; it does not resolve symbolic links
Relying only on client-side filename validation
verification_focus: Can any externally controlled path segment resolve outside the intended canonical base directory at the file-operation sink?

consequence_chains.consequence: relative path traversal reads or writes outside the restricted directory

consequence_chains.trigger: input is an absolute path such as '/etc/passwd' or 'C:\\Windows\\win.ini'
consequence_chains.consequence: absolute path traversal bypasses the configured base directory

consequence_chains.trigger: validated path later resolves through a symbolic link
consequence_chains.consequence: symlink escape reaches files outside the restricted directory

consequence_chains.trigger: attacker controls upload destination path and file content
consequence_chains.consequence: arbitrary file placement can lead to code execution

patch_principle: Canonicalize or resolve the base and target paths before authorization and before file access.
Reject the target unless its canonical path remains under the canonical base directory.
Prefer fixed ID-to-file mappings or strict filename allowlists over accepting raw paths.
Reject absolute paths, parent-directory elements, directory separators, and unexpected extensions when only filenames are required.
Handle symbolic links explicitly with toRealPath(), realpath(), or NOFOLLOW_LINKS as appropriate.

minimal_examples.safe: Path b=base.toRealPath(); Path p=b.resolve(name).toRealPath(LinkOption.NOFOLLOW_LINKS); if(!p.startsWith(b)) throw new SecurityException(); Files.delete(p);
